bib.title: Self-Evaluation Guided Beam Search for Reasoning
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2023 (37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

read.skipped: References skimmed; GPT-4 qualitative appendix figure text and prompt tables 7-15 only skimmed

question: Can stepwise LLM self-evaluation guide a stochastic beam search over reasoning steps to reduce error accumulation in multi-step reasoning?
hypothesis: Step-level self-evaluated correctness confidence is a better-calibrated criterion than generation probability alone, and guiding decoding with it improves multi-step reasoning, especially for long chains.
contributions: Stepwise self-evaluation (multiple-choice P(A)) as a constraint combined with LM probability in a decoding objective
Stochastic beam search with temperature tau and decay alpha over reasoning steps
Gains on arithmetic, symbolic and commonsense benchmarks with Codex; cost-matched gains with Llama-2 13B
Analysis showing self-evaluation pinpoints logic failures and helps more on longer chains

method.summary: Each reasoning step (a CoT sentence or PAL line) is a decoding unit. For each of k beams, n step candidates are sampled from the generator; the same LLM, prompted with few-shot multiple-choice evaluation exemplars, scores each step's correctness C = P(option A). Candidates are scored by E = prod P^lambda C^(1-lambda) and k beams are sampled without replacement from softmax(E/tau). Final answer by majority vote over final beam.

inference.decoding: stepwise stochastic beam search; beam pruning by sampling k without replacement from P_beam proportional to exp(E/tau)
inference.temperature: generation gamma: Codex PAL 0.4-0.8, Codex CoT 0.1-0.5, Llama-2 PAL <=0.5, CoT >0.5; sampling tau=0.5 PAL, 0.2 CoT; tau=0 deterministic single chain
inference.samples: Codex k=5, n=16 rollouts per beam; Llama-2 n=2, k in [3,4] (k up to 10 in Fig 6a); majority vote over final beam from <=10 searches
inference.prompting: Generation: baseline CoT/PAL few-shot exemplars (GSM8K CoT 8-shot). Evaluation: multiple-choice 'Is the above step of reasoning (A) Correct (B) Incorrect', manual few-shot exemplars from baseline outputs on training data (GSM8K CoT 5-shot). Same backend LLM for both.

evidence.quote: We set k = 5, n = 16 with Codex backbone to balance the quality and efficiency.

results.claim: Codex PAL guided beam search beats PAL-SC on GSM8K in multi-chain setting
results.setup: GSM8K, Codex, multiple chains, k=5 n=16
results.quote: by guiding the reasoning decoding process of the Codex model (Chen et al., 2021), we achieve accuracies of 85.5%, 64.2%, and 77.2% on the GSM8K, AQuA, and StrategyQA benchmarks, compared to the vanilla reasoning-enhanced Codex performance of 80.4%, 58.6%, and 73.2%, respectively.
on StrategyQA, we achieve an accuracy of 77.2% compared with 73.2% of the baseline.

results.setup: Codex, tau=0 single chain vs PAL 72.0 -> 80.2
results.quote: we observe absolute increases in accuracy of 5.3%, 8.3%, and 0.7% on GSM8K, AQuA, and SVAMP,
results.note: Table 1: 80.2 vs 72.0 (8.2 points); text says 5.3 which appears to compare against another baseline, unclear

results.claim: Cost cost-matched: Llama-2 13B PAL GSM8K beats PAL-SC at lower token cost
results.setup: Llama-2 13B, PAL, multiple chains, n=2; 12.6k tokens vs 13.9k
results.quote: we achieve 46.1% on GSM8K with a cost of 12.6k tokens, compared with the accuracy of 41.8% of self-consistency which costs 13.9k tokens.

results.claim: Overhead: single-chain PAL costs about 3x self-consistency on GSM8K at n=16
results.table: Table 1, row Ours-PAL single reasoning chain, column # Tokens

results.claim: Gains grow with chain length on GSM8K (>=9 steps)
StrategyQA gain concentrated in long chains (>=5 steps)
Using only correctness confidence (lambda=1) lowers GSM8K accuracy
results.setup: Codex PAL GSM8K, vs 80.2 at lambda=0.5; lambda=0 gives 77.1
results.quote: when setting λ to 1 (E = C) or 0 (E = P), the performance on GSM8K decreases from 80.2% to 74.5% and 77.1%, respectively.

results.claim: Beam size: multi-chain majority over final beam 42.8% at k=10 vs 35.7% single
Method lags CoT baseline on short commonsense chains with Llama-2 StrategyQA
No gain when baseline strong: Object Counting
results.quote: when the baseline itself performs well on the task (e.g., 96.7% on Object Counting), our approach may not

limits: Needs token logits, so unusable with GPT-4/ChatGPT-style APIs (authors)
Extra cost from candidate sampling and self-evaluation; best for longer chains (authors)
Little gain when baseline already confident/low diversity (Object Counting, Sports)
Weaker on short chains: below CoT at equal cost on commonsense with Llama-2
Correctness confidence barely separates correct from wrong on StrategyQA; plausible-but-wrong chains score high (Fig 7b R41)
Self-evaluation is by the same model; no seeds or significance tests; Codex deprecated
Only two Llama-2 13B cost studies; k=5, n=16 headline results cost ~3x to ~75x baseline tokens
